html:
SMTO-BOOT-0040 — The model software isn't using your NVIDIA graphics card

GUID: 4e3b796f-9949-49c2-b497-749c2396bf21
Slug: boot-vllm-backend-invalid
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • Your graphics card passed its tests, but vLLM, the software that runs local models, didn't switch to its NVIDIA mode. The environment stays installed but isn't ready to run models.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Run ./src/vllm/install-vllm.sh --verify-only followed by the name of the environment you use for models (vllm by default). Checking a different environment from the one you run models in can give a misleading result.
  2. If it fails again, create a fresh environment under a new name, for example ./src/vllm/install-vllm.sh vllm2, then run --verify-only on that name. The installer picks vLLM and PyTorch versions that match your card, and it won't reuse an existing name.
  3. If you run this inside a container or limit which graphics cards are visible, ask the person who manages it to make the NVIDIA cards available. vLLM only picks its NVIDIA mode when it can see the cards directly.

What success looks like

  • The check finishes and prints “vLLM verification complete.”

If it still fails

  • Send the error code and the full terminal output, including the line listing the vLLM, PyTorch and CUDA versions, to the person who maintains your model setup. Don't launch models from this environment until the check passes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • install-vllm.sh verification found vllm.platforms.current_platform.is_cuda() false after the PyTorch CUDA checks passed, so vLLM did not select its CUDA backend.

What this means

  • Installed vLLM's current_platform reports that CUDA is not its selected backend. Final verification stops because vLLM's selected platform is not CUDA. The environment and installed packages remain. The platform result alone does not identify whether the installed build, device visibility or environment selection caused it.

Why this can happen

  • Installed vLLM's current_platform reports that CUDA is not its selected backend.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the actual vLLM/PyTorch environment and device visibility rather than changing a model path.

How to fix it

  • Confirm you verified the intended environment (./src/vllm/install-vllm.sh --verify-only with its name), that the installed vllm wheel is a CUDA build matching the PyTorch CUDA version in the version line, and that NVIDIA devices and NVML are visible to the process (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, container GPU passthrough). If the build is wrong, install into a new environment name with install-vllm.sh, which selects matching vLLM and PyTorch CUDA builds, and require --verify-only to pass before launching a model.
  • Verify the installed vLLM build and authorized GPU access in the intended environment.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the selected vLLM environment and CUDA access, then require --verify-only to pass before launching a model.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended verified environment selects its CUDA backend.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Final verification stops because vLLM's selected platform is not CUDA. The environment and installed packages remain.
  • The platform result alone does not identify whether the installed build, device visibility or environment selection caused it.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
